file: Luther at the Diet of Worms.jpg
caption: Martin Luther before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms, April 1521, as imagined by a nineteenth-century painter.
credit: Anton von Werner (1843–1915), Luther at the Diet of Worms, 1877

caption: The Joseph Smith birthplace memorial at Sharon, Vermont, with the granite obelisk dedicated in December 1905, as published in 1907.
credit: Photographer unknown; published in the Improvement Era, December 1907

caption: The grove west of the Smith farm in Manchester, New York, known to Latter-day Saints as the Sacred Grove, photographed about 1907.
The hill about three miles from the Smith farm, now called the Hill Cumorah, photographed in 1907.

file: Joseph Smith family farm in Manchester.jpg
caption: The Smith family farm in Manchester, New York, the land Alvin worked to pay for, photographed about 1907.

file: The Hill Cumorah by C.C.A. Christensen.jpeg
caption: The angel Moroni and Joseph Smith at the hill, as C.C.A. Christensen painted the scene in the nineteenth century.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), The Hill Cumorah, 19th century

file: Tarring and Feathering the Prophet by C.C.A. Christensen.PNG
caption: Hiram, Ohio, March 1832: the mob drags Joseph from the Johnson home at night, as Christensen painted it.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Tarring and Feathering the Prophet, 19th century

file: Saints Driven From Jackson County Missouri by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: November 1833: Latter-day Saints driven from Jackson County, Missouri, in Christensen's painting.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Saints Driven from Jackson County, Missouri, 19th century

file: Lower Auditorium Temple, Kirtland, Ohio LCCN93506504.jpg
after: Joseph never spoke publicly about this vision
caption: The Melchizedek Priesthood pulpits at the west end of the Kirtland Temple's lower hall, photographed in 1912, with a curtain rolled up overhead. It was behind curtains at these upper pulpits that Joseph and Oliver knelt on April 3, 1836.
credit: C. Edward Miller, photograph, copyrighted 1912; Library of Congress

file: The Arrest of Mormon Leaders by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: Far West, Missouri, October 31, 1838: Joseph and other leaders taken prisoner under a flag of truce, as Christensen painted it.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), The Arrest of Mormon Leaders, 19th century

caption: Winter 1838–39: Latter-day Saint families leave Missouri for Illinois.
The jail at Liberty, Missouri, where Joseph and his companions were held through the winter of 1838–39, in Christensen's painting.

file: Nauvoo Illinois ca 1846 with Temple on hill.png
caption: Nauvoo about 1846, with the temple on the bluff in the distance. One of the earliest photographs of the city.

file: The Nauvoo Temple by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: The Nauvoo Temple on the bluff above the city, as Christensen painted it.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), The Nauvoo Temple, 19th century

file: Joseph Mustering the Nauvoo Legion by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: Joseph Smith with the Nauvoo Legion, in Christensen's painting.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Joseph Mustering the Nauvoo Legion, 19th century

file: Exterior of Carthage Jail by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: Carthage Jail, June 27, 1844, as Christensen painted it decades later, with a shaft of light at the window where Joseph fell.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Exterior of Carthage Jail, 19th century

file: Crossing the Mississippi on the Ice by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: The Saints leave Nauvoo across the frozen Mississippi in February 1846, with the city and temple behind them.
